questions.question: The famous Indus Valley site of Dholavira is located in which present-day Indian state?
questions.explanation: Dholavira is in the Rann of Kachchh, Gujarat. It is known for sophisticated water management and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.

questions.question: Who among the following was the court poet of Samudragupta and composed the Allahabad Pillar Inscription (Prayag Prashasti)?
questions.explanation: Harisena composed the Prayag Prashasti in Sanskrit, detailing Samudragupta's conquests. Banabhatta was Harsha's biographer; Ravikirti wrote the Aihole inscription for Pulakeshin II.

questions.question: The 'Market Control Policy' fixing prices of commodities was introduced by which Delhi Sultan?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Khalji fixed prices (rate lists), set up separate markets (shahna-i-mandi), and used spies to enforce controls — mainly to maintain a large army cheaply.

questions.question:
Arrange chronologically:
1. Battle of Buxar
2. Battle of Plassey
3. Grant of Diwani of Bengal
4. Regulating Act
questions.explanation: Plassey (1757) → Buxar (1764) → Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa granted to the Company (1765) → Regulating Act (1773).

questions.question: The Lucknow Pact (1916) is significant because:
options: Congress and Muslim League agreed to joint constitutional demands
It introduced separate electorates for the first time
questions.explanation: At Lucknow, the INC (with reunited Moderates & Extremists) and the Muslim League jointly demanded self-government; Congress accepted separate electorates (first introduced earlier by Morley-Minto Reforms, 1909).

questions.question: Which session of the Indian National Congress adopted the resolution of 'Purna Swaraj'?
questions.explanation: The Lahore Session (Dec 1929), presided by Jawaharlal Nehru, adopted Purna Swaraj as the goal. 26 January 1930 was observed as the first Independence Day.

questions.question: The Gandhara school of art flourished under which dynasty and shows influence of which foreign style?
questions.explanation: The Gandhara school (1st–5th century CE) flourished under the Kushanas (esp. Kanishka) with strong Greco-Roman (Hellenistic) influence — Buddha in wavy hair, drapery. Used grey schist.

questions.question: Who founded the 'Servants of India Society' in 1905?
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune to train national missionaries for social service and promote the interests of Indians by constitutional means.

questions.question: During the Quit India Movement, parallel governments were established at several places. 'Jatiya Sarkar' was set up at:
questions.explanation: Tamluk (Midnapore, Bengal) — Jatiya Sarkar under Satish Samanta. Satara had 'Prati Sarkar' (Nana Patil); Ballia under Chittu Pandey was among the earliest.

questions.question: The Vijayanagara empire's 'Amara-Nayaka' system closely resembled:
options: The Iqta system of the Delhi Sultanate
questions.explanation: Amara-Nayakas were military chiefs assigned territories (amaram) for revenue collection in return for troops and tribute — functionally similar to iqtas of the Sultanate.

questions.question: The catastrophic nuclear accident in Ukraine in 1986 occurred at which power plant?
questions.explanation: The 1986 accident occurred at Unit 4 of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, in what is now Ukraine.

questions.question: The Battle of the Somme in World War I took place in which country?
questions.explanation: The Battle of the Somme was fought in Picardy, France, from July to November 1916.

questions.question: In which war did the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki occur?
questions.explanation: The United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945, during World War II.

questions.question: Who was the first United States president born after the Declaration of Independence?
questions.explanation: Martin Van Buren, born in New York in 1782, was the first U.S. president born after the Declaration of Independence.

questions.question: Which mammal was the first animal to orbit Earth?
questions.explanation: Laika, a dog aboard Sputnik 2, became the first animal to orbit Earth in 1957.

questions.question: Which Renaissance artist sculpted the marble statue David, now in Florence's Galleria dell'Accademia?
questions.explanation: Michelangelo was commissioned to make David in 1501; the work is in Florence's Galleria dell'Accademia.

questions.question: Which architectural feature is a defining characteristic of the Gothic style?
questions.explanation: Pointed arches are an important characteristic of Gothic architecture and were used in features such as arcades, vaults, doors, and windows.

questions.question: The Creation of Adam, one of the central frescoes of the Sistine Chapel ceiling, was painted by which artist?
questions.explanation: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling; The Creation of Adam is one of its central Genesis scenes.

questions.question: Picasso's 1937 painting Guernica was inspired by the bombing of Gernika during which conflict?
questions.explanation: The bombing of the Basque town of Gernika took place during the Spanish Civil War and inspired Picasso's Guernica.

questions.question: In what year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989; German reunification followed in 1990.

questions.question: Which ship carried the Pilgrims across the Atlantic in 1620?
questions.explanation: The Mayflower left for America in 1620 and brought the Pilgrims to Cape Cod.

questions.question: Which treaty was signed at Versailles on 28 June 1919 between the Allied and Associated Powers and Germany?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed by the Allied and Associated Powers and Germany at Versailles on 28 June 1919.

questions.question: In what year did the First World War begin?
questions.explanation: The war began in 1914 after Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia on 28 July, followed by German declarations in August.

questions.question: In Greek mythology, Poseidon was the god of which realm?
questions.explanation: Poseidon was the Greek god of the sea and was commonly identified by his trident.

questions.question: Which Greek god is associated with wine?
questions.explanation: Dionysus was the Greek god of wine and was honoured through festivals that also featured theatre.

questions.question: Which figure from Greek mythology descended to the Underworld to recover Eurydice?
questions.explanation: Orpheus descended to the Underworld to recover his wife Eurydice and persuaded its rulers to restore her to life.

questions.question: In Greek religion, who was Zeus's sister-wife and queen of the Olympian gods?
questions.explanation: Hera was Zeus's sister-wife and the queen of the Olympian gods; the Romans identified her with Juno.

questions.question: Which agricultural policy did Joseph Stalin promote during the First Five-Year Plan?
options: Removal of state control over agriculture
questions.explanation: Stalin's First Five-Year Plan sought to transform largely individual farms into large state collective farms through collectivization.

questions.question: At the Battle of Hastings, what defensive formation did Harold's army form on the hilltop?
questions.explanation: The English formed a shield wall, locking shields together on the hilltop to resist the Norman attack.

questions.question: Which tactic did the Normans use at the Battle of Hastings to draw English troops away from the shield wall?
questions.explanation: The Normans pretended to flee, encouraging some English soldiers to break ranks and pursue before Norman cavalry counter-attacked.
